reasons: Classification is correct: the only liability limitation (p0077) caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting/support compensation while Client's liability — notably the sweeping Section 12(a) indemnity covering 'any breach by Client of this Agreement' — is uncapped. That is expressly walk-away territory under LOL-CAP ('Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped') and fails the mutual-cap fallback, so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted, not over-flagging.

Redline reaches the preferred position on the material terms: it makes the cap mutual, extends it Agreement-wide rather than the ambiguous 'Section 3, 4, 7 and 11', sets the basis at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, adds a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and adds a single Excluded Claims sentence covering confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, while preserving Client's payment obligations outside the limitation.

The vendor's original gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct exception is not lost — it is reproduced (and made mutual) inside Excluded Claims — so the edit does not silently strip counterparty-adverse language or benefit the counterparty.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.80 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here: converting a one-sided, cross-reference-limited cap into a mutual Agreement-wide cap with a floor, a damages exclusion and a carve-out definition necessarily rewrites the sentence; the drafter still edited the existing clause rather than adding a new section.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states what changed, why (unlimited Client exposure via the Section 12(a) indemnity), cites the preferred position and offers the 12-month-fees fallback.

Minor points to confirm rather than blockers: (i) the cross-references 'this Section 12' and 'Section 5' are asserted but not evidenced in the supplied paragraphs and should be checked against the executed numbering; (ii) because Section 12(a)(i) indemnifies 'any breach by Client', the uncapped indemnification carve-out leaves much of Client's exposure outside the new cap — consider limiting that carve-out to third-party indemnity claims in negotiation, though as drafted it tracks the playbook's stated position.
